# DRAFT: Certifier statement on disaster relationship

> **Draft prepared by Counted for review. Not a death certificate. Not valid until reviewed and signed by the
> certifying medical examiner, coroner or physician.**

| | |
|---|---|
| Case | 50e70bdc626c |
| Decedent | age unknown, sex not stated |
| Date of death | 2021-02-18 |
| Location | Fort Bend County, TX |
| Disaster | Severe Winter Storms (DR-4586-TX); incident period 2021-02-11 to 2021-02-21 |
| NWS warnings in force | Winter Storm Watch (2021-02-14), Winter Storm Warning (2021-02-14), Hard Freeze Warning (2021-02-15), Hard Freeze Watch (2021-02-15), Wind Chill Watch (2021-02-15) |
| Cause on certificate (per family) | not known |

## Determination (CDC 2017 Reference Guide)
The information gathered does **not** support attributing this death to Severe Winter Storms (DR-4586-TX).

**Causal chain:** Decedent had a ten-year history of Alzheimer's disease and died in a nursing home that maintained normal operations with generator backup throughout the February 2021 Texas winter storm; no disruption to her care, utilities, or medical management was reported, and no credible pathway from the disaster to her death has been identified.

**Proposed "How injury occurred" (Item 43):** n/a

**Proposed wording for FEMA Funeral Assistance** (FEMA rejects "may have been caused by"):
> Not applicable.

## Family account (verbatim)
- none recorded

# Funeral Assistance: what to gather

We are very sorry for your loss. FEMA may help with funeral costs when a death was caused directly or indirectly by a declared disaster.

Good news: FEMA Individual Assistance was approved for Fort Bend County under DR-4586-TX. Funeral Assistance is part of that program.

- [ ] Death certificate, OR the signed certifier statement Counted drafted (ask the medical examiner or doctor to review and sign it)
- [ ] Funeral home contract or itemized receipts
- [ ] Proof of any other help received (insurance, burial societies, donations)
- [ ] The decedent's and applicant's names and addresses

Apply at DisasterAssistance.gov or call 1-800-621-3362. If FEMA says no, you can appeal in writing using the appeal letter below.

_Counted cannot promise any outcome. FEMA makes the decision._
